desk.headline: Revenue up 13% to $8.8bn and adjusted EPS up 21% to $1.94, beat; 2026 adjusted EPS outlook raised to about $4.70 on the call
results: Operating revenue rose 13% to $8.8bn; reported earnings were $2.0bn ($1.77 a share) against $1.7bn ($1.55).
Excluding wind-repowering depreciation, debt buyback costs and other items, EPS rose 21% to $1.94.
Warmer weather, higher usage and customer growth, and more sales to large commercial and industrial users drove the gain; higher operating costs, taxes and new shares held it back.
Weather-adjusted retail sales grew 3.5%, led by commercial (+7.3%); Georgia Power profit rose 22% to $1.52bn.
Nine-month adjusted EPS is $4.40, up from $3.76. The press release itself gives no outlook.

guidance.summary: The press release has no outlook. On the call, as reported, Southern lifted its 2026 adjusted EPS expectation to about $4.70 from its original $4.50–4.60 range, implying roughly $0.30 for Q4.

points: Data-centre electricity use rose 59% y/y in the quarter; signed large-load contracts reach 21 GW, with about 7 GW more in late-stage talks.
The base capital plan is $81bn plus about $4bn of extra projects, and management said the five-year plan could approach $100bn.
About $2bn of new equity is still needed through 2030; the company targets 17% FFO-to-debt by 2029.
Base rates in Alabama and Georgia are held flat until at least 2029; a major Georgia rate case is expected in 2028.
Risks flagged in coverage: political pushback on new Georgia data centres, rising generation build costs and share dilution.
call.source: Call coverage: GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance, 5 Nov 2026; Securities.io, 5 Nov 2026 (no prepared remarks filed)

watch: Conversion of the late-stage large-load pipeline into signed contracts.
Any update to the capital plan and the related equity funding.
Initial 2027 earnings guidance, likely with Q4 results.
